rules.title: Account creation without in-app account deletion
rules.summary: Apps that support account creation must let people start deleting the account from inside the app, not only by email or a website hidden behind support. Apps using Sign in with Apple must also revoke the user's tokens when the account is deleted.
rules.fix: Add a clearly labeled delete-account action in account settings. Confirm, then delete the account and its data, or explain the timeline if regulations require retention. For Sign in with Apple, call the REST API to revoke tokens.
review: Can a signed-in person reach account deletion from the app's settings in a few taps?
Does deletion remove the account and its data, not just sign out or deactivate?
Are Sign in with Apple tokens revoked on deletion?

rules.title: Login-gated app without demo credentials for App Review
rules.summary: Guideline 2.1 asks for demo account details when the app has a login, with the backend running during review. A missing or broken demo account is one of the most common 2.1 rejections.
rules.fix: Fill in Sign-in Information under App Review Information in App Store Connect with a working account that exposes every feature, including paid ones. If login needs a code or hardware, explain how to get past it in the review notes or provide a demo mode.
review: Does the demo account work right now, and will it still work in two weeks?
Does it unlock every feature the reviewer needs to see, including subscriptions?

rules.title: Login required for features that do not need an account
rules.summary: Guideline 5.1.1(v): if the app lacks significant account-based features, people must be able to use it without logging in. Requiring personal data that the core function does not need is also not allowed.
rules.fix: Let people browse and use non-account features before signing in. Ask for sign-in only at the feature that needs it.
review: Can a new person do anything useful before creating an account?
Does every required sign-up field serve a core feature or a legal requirement?

rules.title: Third-party login without a privacy-preserving alternative
rules.summary: Apps that use a third-party or social login service, such as Google or Facebook, to set up the primary account must also offer an equivalent login that limits collection to name and email, lets people keep their email private, and does not track without consent. Sign in with Apple meets all three.
rules.fix: Add Sign in with Apple, or another service with the same privacy properties, alongside the existing social logins, with equal prominence.
review: Does the equivalent login appear with the same prominence as the social logins?
Is the app exempt, for example a client for the developer's own account system or an enterprise or education app?

rules.title: App Store icon missing or has transparency
rules.summary: The app needs a 1024 by 1024 App Store icon in its asset catalog, without an alpha channel. A missing or transparent marketing icon fails upload validation.
rules.fix: Add a 1024 by 1024 opaque PNG to the AppIcon set, or design it in Icon Composer, and archive again.

rules.title: Development endpoints shipped in the release build
rules.summary: URLs pointing at localhost, private network addresses, tunnels, or staging hosts in the release build usually mean a feature that fails for the reviewer, which is a 2.1 completeness rejection.
rules.fix: Move environment URLs behind build configurations and make sure the Release configuration points at production.

rules.title: Deployment target below iOS 13
rules.summary: Since September 9, 2026, iOS and iPadOS apps uploaded to App Store Connect must target iOS 13 or later.
rules.fix: Raise `IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` to 13.0 or later for the app and every embedded extension and framework.

rules.title: Code downloaded or loaded at runtime
rules.summary: Apps must be self-contained and may not download, install, or execute code that adds or changes features. `dlopen` on a downloaded path, loading bundles from the Documents folder, or evaluating remote scripts that drive native features are red flags. Interpreted code that runs in WebKit or JavaScriptCore is allowed when it does not change the app's primary purpose.
rules.fix: Ship features in the binary and gate them with local flags. Keep remote content to data, not code.
review: Does any downloaded content add features or change what the app does, beyond data and web content?

rules.title: No launch screen configured
rules.summary: iPhone and iPad apps must provide a launch screen through `UILaunchScreen` or `UILaunchStoryboardName`. Without one the app runs letterboxed on modern devices and the upload is rejected.
rules.fix: Add a `UILaunchScreen` dictionary to Info.plist, or the Launch Screen section in the target's Info tab.

rules.title: Non-public API or private framework in use
rules.summary: Apps may use public APIs only. Linking a private framework, calling underscore-prefixed or undocumented selectors, or reaching private classes through `NSClassFromString` or `perform(_:)` leads to rejection, often by automated binary scanning.
rules.fix: Replace the call with a public API. If a dependency does it, update or replace the dependency.

rules.title: macOS bundle contains quarantined files
rules.summary: Since February 18, 2025, macOS apps must not include files carrying the `com.apple.quarantine` extended attribute, which usually comes from resources downloaded and copied into the project.
rules.fix: Remove the attribute from the source files with `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine <path>`, then archive again.

rules.title: Built with an SDK older than App Store Connect accepts
rules.summary: Since April 28, 2026, new apps and updates must be built with the iOS 26, iPadOS 26, tvOS 26, visionOS 26, or watchOS 26 SDK, which means Xcode 26 or later. Older builds are rejected at upload.
rules.fix: Build and archive with Xcode 26 or later. The deployment target can stay lower; only the SDK must be current.

rules.title: Name, icon, or UI copies another app or an Apple product
rules.summary: Apps may not copy another developer's name, icon, brand, or UI, and may not look confusingly similar to Apple products, interfaces, or apps.
rules.fix: Use an original name and icon, and check them against the App Store and a trademark search before submitting.
review: Does a search for the app name show another app with the same or a confusable name or icon?
Does any screen imitate an Apple app or system UI closely enough to be mistaken for it?

rules.title: iPhone app does not hold up on iPad
rules.summary: iPhone apps should run on iPad whenever possible, and App Review tests iPhone-only apps on iPad too. Clipped layouts or crashes there count against the submission.
rules.fix: Support iPad in the target, or at least test the iPhone app in compatibility mode on an iPad simulator before submitting.
review: Does every screen lay out and work on the smallest and largest iPad?

rules.title: App duplicates the developer's other apps or a saturated category
rules.summary: Guideline 4.3 rejects multiple bundle IDs for the same app, apps indistinguishable from what is widely available, and template-based apps. Since June 2026, existing apps that are not updated, improved, or attracting customers may also be removed.
rules.fix: Merge variants into one app with in-app choices. In the review notes, state what is distinctive about the app compared with the category.
review: Does the developer account have another app with the same core function?
What does this app do that the top apps in its category do not?
Is it built from a commercial template or app generator?

rules.title: App is mostly a wrapped website
rules.summary: Apps must offer features, content, and UI beyond a repackaged website. An app whose main screen is a `WKWebView` loading the developer's site, with little native functionality, is rejected for minimum functionality.
rules.fix: Build the core flows natively and use platform capabilities the website cannot, such as offline use, widgets, notifications, or system integrations.
review: Is there meaningful native functionality beyond the web content?

rules.title: Accessibility Nutrition Labels not declared
rules.summary: Accessibility Nutrition Labels show on the product page which features, such as VoiceOver, Larger Text, or Sufficient Contrast, the app supports for its common tasks. Declaring them is voluntary today, and Apple has said it will become required over time.
rules.fix: Test the common tasks with each feature, then declare the supported ones per device in App Store Connect under Accessibility.

rules.title: Age rating questionnaire incomplete or inaccurate
rules.summary: App Store ratings now include 13+, 16+, and 18+, with new required questions on in-app controls, capabilities, medical or wellness topics, and violent themes. Updates cannot be submitted until the new questionnaire is answered, and inaccurate answers draw 2.3.6 rejections.
rules.fix: Answer the updated age rating questionnaire in App Store Connect honestly, covering user-generated content, web access, and AI chat features.
review: Do the answers account for user-generated content, unrestricted web access, and AI-generated content?

rules.title: EU trader status not provided
rules.summary: Under the EU Digital Services Act, every developer must declare whether they are a trader to distribute in the European Union. Traders must also verify an address, phone number, and email, which appear on the product page. Apps without a declaration are removed from EU storefronts.
rules.fix: Set the trader status under Business in App Store Connect and complete verification if you are a trader.

rules.title: Encryption export compliance not declared
rules.summary: Without `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption` in Info.plist, App Store Connect asks the export compliance questions for every build, and the build waits until someone answers.
rules.fix: Set `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption` to `false` if the app uses only exempt encryption, such as HTTPS and Apple's system APIs. Otherwise answer the questions and upload the documentation.

rules.title: Apple trademarks used in the app name or icon
rules.summary: Apps may not look confusingly similar to Apple products or imply Apple endorsement. Using Apple trademarks such as iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Siri, or App Store as part of the app name, or Apple product images in the icon, is a common rejection.
rules.fix: Use Apple trademarks only referentially in the description, for example "for iPhone". Keep them out of the name and icon.
review: Does the icon use an Apple product image or an Apple glyph?

rules.title: Store text exceeds App Store Connect limits
rules.summary: App Store Connect caps the subtitle at 30 characters, keywords at 100 bytes, promotional text at 170 characters, and the description and What's New text at 4,000 characters each, per localization.
rules.fix: Trim the field. Keywords count bytes, so non-Latin scripts fit fewer characters; separate them with commas and no spaces.

rules.title: Name or subtitle carries prices, rankings, or unverifiable claims
rules.summary: Names, subtitles, screenshots, and previews may not include prices, terms that do not describe the app, or unverifiable claims such as "best" or "#1", and may not pack popular app names or trademarks.
rules.fix: Describe what the app does in plain words. Move prices and offers to promotional text.

rules.title: App name longer than 30 characters
rules.summary: App names are limited to 30 characters. App Store Connect refuses longer names for every localization.
rules.fix: Shorten the name and move descriptive words to the subtitle or keywords.

rules.title: Store text mentions other platforms
rules.summary: Metadata must focus on the Apple platforms the app supports and not mention other mobile platforms or their stores.
rules.fix: Remove references to other platforms and stores, unless the app's core function is interoperating with them.

rules.title: Placeholder or test content in the app or its metadata
rules.summary: Submissions must be final: placeholder text, empty web pages, and temporary content must be gone. Lorem ipsum, TODO strings, or "test" entries in String Catalogs or store text are rejected under 2.1.
rules.fix: Replace every placeholder with final copy in each shipped localization, and check that every URL in the metadata opens a real page.

rules.title: Review notes do not explain non-obvious features
rules.summary: Guideline 2.3.1 forbids hidden, dormant, or undocumented features, and asks for every new feature and in-app purchase to be described with specificity in the Notes for Review. Remote feature flags, region-locked features, hardware dependencies, and special configuration all need explaining.
rules.fix: List each feature that is not obvious from the first launch, how to reach it, and any account, location, or hardware it needs. Mention remote configuration and what it can change.
review: Is every feature that needs an account, a location, a device, or a flag described in the notes?
Can remote configuration turn on anything the reviewer did not see?

rules.title: Screenshots missing, mis-sized, or not showing the app in use
rules.summary: App Store Connect needs at least one screenshot in an accepted size for each supported device family. Screenshots must show the app in use, not just title art, a login page, or a splash screen, and must not show features the build lacks.
rules.fix: Capture real screens from the submitted build for every supported device family, such as iPhone and iPad, and keep marketing text to a caption.
review: Does every screenshot show a screen that exists in this build?
Is any screenshot only a splash, login, or title-art frame?

rules.title: Support URL missing, broken, or without contact details
rules.summary: The Support URL must load and give people an easy way to reach the developer. Broken pages and pages with no contact path draw 1.5 and 2.1 rejections.
rules.fix: Point the Support URL at a live page with an email address or contact form, and keep it reachable without signing in.
review: Does the support page show an email address or a contact form?

rules.title: What's New text does not describe the changes
rules.summary: What's New must describe new features and product changes. Generic text is fine only for bug fixes, security updates, and performance improvements.
rules.fix: List the user-visible changes in the release notes for each localization.
review: Does this release add or change a feature the release notes do not mention?

rules.title: App Transport Security disabled globally
rules.summary: `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads` turns off App Transport Security for every connection. App Review asks for a justification, and plain HTTP exposes user data.
rules.fix: Remove the global exception. Use HTTPS, or add a narrow `NSExceptionDomains` entry for the specific host that cannot, and explain it in the review notes.
review: Which hosts cannot use HTTPS, and is the exception limited to them?

rules.title: Hard-coded IPv4 addresses
rules.summary: Apps must work on IPv6-only networks, which App Review uses. Connecting to IPv4 literals or using IPv4-only socket APIs fails there.
rules.fix: Connect by hostname with `URLSession` or `Network.framework`, which handle NAT64 automatically.

rules.title: Digital content may be sold outside in-app purchase
rules.summary: The app links a general payment SDK, such as Stripe or PayPal, or opens checkout URLs. Unlocking features, content, or subscriptions inside the app must use in-app purchase unless an exception in 3.1.3 applies, such as physical goods and services consumed outside the app, reader apps, or storefront-specific entitlements.
rules.fix: Route digital unlocks through StoreKit. Keep the external processor only for physical goods, real-world services, or a storefront where you hold the matching entitlement, and say which exception applies in the review notes.
review: Does anything bought outside in-app purchase unlock content or features inside the app?
If yes, which 3.1.3 exception or storefront entitlement covers it?

rules.title: On-device receipt validation that may reject current receipts
rules.summary: App Store receipts are signed with a SHA-256 intermediate certificate since January 24, 2025. Hand-rolled on-device receipt validation that pins the old certificate or algorithm treats valid purchases as invalid, so the reviewer cannot unlock paid content.
rules.fix: Verify purchases with StoreKit 2 `Transaction` and `AppTransaction`, which handle signing for you. If you must validate receipts yourself, support SHA-256.

rules.title: Restorable purchases without a restore mechanism
rules.summary: The app sells non-consumables or subscriptions but has no visible way to restore them. Guideline 3.1.1 expects a restore mechanism for any restorable in-app purchase.
rules.fix: Add a Restore Purchases action that calls `AppStore.sync()`, or use the StoreKit views, which include it. Place it where people look for it: the paywall and settings.

rules.title: Subscription terms not clearly disclosed
rules.summary: Auto-renewable subscriptions must provide ongoing value, last at least seven days, and state clearly what the person gets, the price, and the billing period before purchase. The app and its metadata must link the Terms of Use (EULA) and the privacy policy.
rules.fix: Show price, period, and what is included on the paywall, with the billed amount as the most prominent price. Link Terms of Use and Privacy Policy on the paywall and in the App Store description or the EULA field.
review: Is the billed amount the most prominent price on the paywall, with any per-week breakdown secondary?
Does the paywall show the trial length and what happens when it ends?
Are Terms of Use and Privacy Policy linked from the paywall?

rules.title: Always-location purpose string without the when-in-use string
rules.summary: `NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription` is set but `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription` is missing. The system needs both to show the upgrade prompt, and the upload is flagged.
rules.fix: Add `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription`. Ask for when-in-use first and request always access only when a feature needs background location.

rules.title: Permissions requested before the person sees why
rules.summary: Guideline 5.1.1(iv) forbids manipulating or forcing consent, and expects alternatives when the person declines. Requesting several permissions at launch, re-prompting after a denial, or blocking the app until access is granted all draw rejections.
rules.fix: Request each permission at the moment the feature needs it. Keep the app usable after a denial: offer a manual alternative, such as typing an address instead of sharing location, and a link to Settings.
review: Does the app ask for any permission before the person starts the feature that needs it?
Does every feature still work, or offer an alternative, after the person declines?
Does any pre-permission screen use only a neutral Continue button, with no dark patterns?

rules.title: Protected resource requested without a purpose string
rules.summary: The app calls an API that requests access to a protected resource, such as the camera, photos, location, or contacts, but its Info.plist lacks the matching purpose string. Upload is rejected, and at runtime the app crashes when it asks.
rules.fix: Add the purpose string key for the resource to Info.plist, or the target's Info tab, with a specific sentence on why the app needs it. Localize it like the rest of the UI.

rules.title: Purpose string is empty, a placeholder, or too vague
rules.summary: Guideline 5.1.1(ii) requires purpose strings that "clearly and completely describe your use of the data". Strings like "This app needs camera access" or a bare product name are among the most common 5.1.1 rejections.
rules.fix: Say what feature uses the data and what the person gets, with an example: "Scan receipts with the camera to add expenses automatically."
review: Does each purpose string name the feature that uses the data and what the person gets from it?

rules.title: App target has no privacy manifest
rules.summary: The app bundle ships without a `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`. Any use of a required reason API, including `UserDefaults`, then fails upload validation, and the App Store privacy report has nothing to aggregate from the app's own code.
rules.fix: Add a `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` to the app target (File > New > File > App Privacy). Declare tracking, collected data types, and every required reason API category the app's own code uses.

rules.title: Privacy policy missing from metadata or the app
rules.summary: Every app needs a privacy policy linked both in the App Store Connect metadata and inside the app, easy to find. The policy must say what data is collected and how, who it is shared with, how long it is kept, and how to revoke consent or request deletion.
rules.fix: Set the Privacy Policy URL in App Store Connect, link the same page from the app's settings or about screen, and make sure the policy covers collection, sharing, retention, deletion, and consent withdrawal.
review: Is the privacy policy reachable from inside the app without signing in?
Does it cover collection, third-party sharing, retention, deletion, and consent withdrawal?

rules.title: Privacy manifest declares an unknown or misplaced reason code
rules.summary: A reason code in `NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypeReasons` is not one Apple lists for that category, or is an SDK-only reason (`0A2A.1`, `C56D.1`) declared by the app itself.
rules.fix: Use only the reason codes Apple lists for each category, and only the ones that describe the real use. Remove SDK-wrapper reasons from the app target's manifest.

rules.title: Required reason API used without a declared reason
rules.summary: Code in the bundle calls an API from a required reason category, such as `UserDefaults`, file timestamps, system boot time, disk space, or active keyboards, and the bundle's privacy manifest does not declare that category. App Store Connect rejects the upload.
rules.fix: Add an `NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes` entry for the category with the approved reason codes that match the real use. Each framework that calls the API needs the declaration in its own manifest; the app's manifest does not cover an SDK.

rules.title: Listed third-party SDK ships without a privacy manifest or signature
rules.summary: The app embeds an SDK from Apple's list of commonly used third-party SDKs, and that copy has no privacy manifest or, as a binary dependency, no valid signature. Uploads of new apps and of updates that add the SDK are rejected.
rules.fix: Update the SDK to a release that includes `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` and, for XCFrameworks, a signature. If no such release exists, replace the SDK.

rules.title: Personal data may be sent to a third-party AI service
rules.summary: The app calls a hosted AI model, such as OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google Gemini. Guideline 5.1.2(i) requires clear disclosure of where personal data goes, including to third-party AI, and explicit permission before sharing it.
rules.fix: Before the first request, show what data goes to which provider and why, and get explicit consent. Mirror it in the privacy policy and the App Privacy details. Prefer on-device models where they do the job.
review: Does the app tell the person which data goes to which AI provider before the first request?
Does the person give explicit permission, and does the app keep working when they decline?

rules.title: Manifest declares tracking without listing tracking domains
rules.summary: `NSPrivacyTracking` is true but `NSPrivacyTrackingDomains` is empty. The system blocks connections to tracking domains until the person grants permission, so undeclared domains keep receiving traffic the person never agreed to.
rules.fix: List every domain that receives tracking data in `NSPrivacyTrackingDomains`, and request App Tracking Transparency permission before contacting them.

rules.title: Kids Category app includes third-party analytics or advertising
rules.summary: Kids Category apps may not include third-party analytics or advertising, with narrow exceptions, may not send personal information or device data to third parties, and must put links out of the app and purchases behind a parental gate.
rules.fix: Remove third-party analytics and ad SDKs, or move the app out of the Kids Category. Add a parental gate before external links and purchases.
review: Is there a parental gate before every external link, purchase, and permission request?

rules.title: Regulated service submitted by an individual developer
rules.summary: Apps in highly regulated fields, such as banking, healthcare, gambling, cannabis, air travel, or crypto exchanges, or apps that need sensitive data, should be submitted by the legal entity that provides the service. Medical apps that could cause harm get extra scrutiny.
rules.fix: Submit from the organization's developer account, and include licenses or regulatory approvals in the review notes.
review: Does the app provide a regulated service, and is the account holder the licensed entity?
For medical features, does the app disclose its data and methods, and are any regulatory clearances available?

rules.title: User-generated content without moderation tools
rules.summary: Apps with user-generated content or social features must filter objectionable material, let people report offensive content with timely responses, let people block abusive users, and publish contact information. Random or anonymous chat apps fall under the same rule.
rules.fix: Ship report and block actions on every piece of user content and every profile, a filtering step, published contact details, and terms that forbid objectionable content.
review: Can a person report any post, comment, or message from where they see it?
Can a person block another user, and does blocking hide that user's content?
Is there a filter for objectionable content, and contact details in the app?

rules.title: Advertising identifier read without App Tracking Transparency
rules.summary: The app or an SDK reads the advertising identifier (`ASIdentifierManager.advertisingIdentifier`) or links an ad or attribution SDK, but never requests tracking permission with `ATTrackingManager`, or has no `NSUserTrackingUsageDescription`.
rules.fix: Request permission with `ATTrackingManager.requestTrackingAuthorization` before any tracking, add the purpose string, and declare tracking in the privacy manifest and App Privacy details. If the app does not track, remove the identifier access.

rules.title: Device signals collected in a way that looks like fingerprinting
rules.summary: Fingerprinting is not allowed, with or without tracking permission. Combining signals such as boot time, disk size, keyboard list, screen metrics, or locale into an identifier, or sending required reason API data off-device, breaks both the guideline and the declared reasons.
rules.fix: Use required reason APIs only for their declared reasons, keep derived values on-device unless the reason allows otherwise, and never combine device signals into an identifier.
review: Does any code or SDK combine device properties into an identifier or send them to a server?

deadlines.title: Approved reasons for required reason APIs
deadlines.summary: Uploads that use required reason APIs without approved reasons in a privacy manifest are rejected.

deadlines.title: EU trader status for app updates
deadlines.summary: Updates to apps distributed in the EU need a trader status declaration.

deadlines.title: SHA-256 receipt signing certificate
deadlines.summary: On-device receipt validation must support the SHA-256 intermediate certificate, or move to AppTransaction and Transaction.

deadlines.title: Privacy manifests and signatures for listed SDKs
deadlines.summary: New apps and updates that add a listed third-party SDK need its privacy manifest and signature.

deadlines.title: EU trader status required to stay on EU storefronts
deadlines.summary: Apps without trader status are removed from the App Store in the EU until verified.

deadlines.title: No quarantine attribute in macOS apps
deadlines.summary: macOS apps must not contain files with the com.apple.quarantine extended attribute.

deadlines.title: Updated age rating questionnaire
deadlines.summary: Updates cannot be submitted until the new age rating questions are answered.

deadlines.title: Xcode 26 and the 26 SDKs
deadlines.summary: New apps and updates must be built with Xcode 26 or later and an SDK for iOS 26, iPadOS 26, tvOS 26, visionOS 26, or watchOS 26.

deadlines.title: iOS 13 minimum deployment target
deadlines.summary: iOS and iPadOS apps uploaded to App Store Connect must target iOS 13 or later.

profiles.summary: Offline tool with no accounts or purchases.
Social or community app with user content.
App built on a hosted AI model.
Banking, payments, lending, or crypto app.

reasons.summary: Display file timestamps to the person using the device; not sent off-device.
Timestamps, size, or metadata of files inside the app, app group, or CloudKit container.
Timestamps, size, or metadata of files the user granted access to, such as via a document picker.
Third-party SDK wrapper called only by the app.
Measure elapsed time between in-app events or drive timers.
Calculate absolute timestamps for in-app events, such as UIKit or AVFAudio events.
Include boot time in an optional, user-submitted bug report.
Display disk space to the person using the device.
Check for enough space to write files, or delete files when space is low.
Include disk space in an optional, user-submitted bug report.
Health research app warning participants about low disk space.
Custom keyboard app whose primary function is a systemwide keyboard.
Present the correct customized UI for the active keyboard in the app's text fields.
Read and write information only the app itself can access.
Read and write information shared within the app's App Group.
Third-party SDK wrapper called only by the app.
Read managed app configuration or write managed feedback for MDM.

traits.summary: People create or sign in to an account.
The app sells anything through StoreKit.
People post, share, or message content other people see.
The app is in the Kids Category or aimed at children.
The app reads or writes health or medical data.
The app handles cryptocurrency wallets, exchanges, or mining.
The app sends data to a hosted AI model or generates content with AI.
The app shows ads or shares data with ad or attribution networks.
The app configures a VPN or network extension.
The app shows web content in a web view.
The app offers a regulated service: banking, lending, healthcare, gambling, or similar.
The app ships on the Mac App Store.

resources.name: Photo library
resources.note: PhotosPicker and PHPickerViewController need no purpose string; prefer them.

resources.name: Contacts
resources.note: ContactAccessPicker and CNContactPickerViewController need no purpose string; prefer them.
